text:
sarah: FYI seeing a weird spike in blocked GPU allocs in us-central1 starting ~09:02 UTC. provisioning queue stuck at 50+ pods.
kevin: seen it, I think something is wedging local disks during snapshot cleanup. nvme SMART errors + trim seems to hang.
maya: logs?
sarah: pasting dmesg from one host:
```
[Fri May 10 09:01:58] nvme0: I/O 0 queued for 120s, controller reset
[Fri May 10 09:02:00] nvme0: reset failed, controller frozen
[Fri May 10 09:02:03] overlayfs: unlinkat failed during delete; errno=5
```
kevin: that errno=5 is I/O error. I also see janitor worker starting deletes + fstrim around same time in traces.
arpit: we had a recent host firmware push last week to us-central1 (nvme fw 3.2.11). could be related.
sarah: infra-bot: marked ~30 nodes as degraded and drained, but scheduler still hitting warm pool and failing attach.
ops-runner: @sarah pushed a temporary policy to avoid scheduling onto nodes with recent scrub_activity tag :gear:
maya: can we throttle the janitor/cleanup on those hosts? current cron runs with concurrency 8.
kevin: yes, reduce to 1 and add random jitter. Also disable concurrent fstrim during deletes; we'll run fstrim in maintenance windows.
sarah: quick mitigation rolled: janitor concurrency -> 1, fstrim disabled via flag on 172 nodes in us-central1. monitor now.
kevin: patch posted to infra-janitor repo, PR #842: add --no-fstrim and --max-concurrency flags.
maya: long term: consider rolling back fw 3.2.11 for affected hardware families until vendor confirms fix.
arpit: vendor acknowledged a TRIM path regression on 3.2.11 in certain controller batches. they're preparing micro-patch.
sarah: metrics: blocked gpu allocs dropped to 6 after throttle, median attach latency down from 2.1s -> 0.6s, still seeing occasional requeue on few hosts.
kevin: plan: keep throttle + rollout firmware rollback for canary rack of 10 nodes tomorrow 02:00 UTC, test heavy batch attach, then expand if green.
maya: adding a temporary routing rule to steer latency-sensitive workloads to other regions for next 24h.
arpit: opened a ticket with vendor (VND-12345) and flagged for priority.
sarah: thanks. I'll keep the thread updated. if anyone sees another host with controller_freeze in dmesg, ping here and include node-id.
kevin: also capturing SMART and nvme-cli logs: `nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0` and `nvme error-log /dev/nvme0` — collect before any reboot.
infra-bot: automated alert suppressed for 30m while throttles take effect :white_check_mark:
maya: good work all, we'll review post-mortem after rollback window. :coffee:
